results.name: Dumbbell Straight Arm Twisting Sit-Up
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell with both hands extended straight above your chest.

Bend your core and lift your upper body off the floor, raising the dumbbell towards the ceiling as high as possible. As you crunch, twist your torso to the right, bringing the dumbbell towards your right side.

Lower your upper body back to the floor with control, maintaining your arms extended above your chest. Repeat the movement, this time twisting to the left. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight and avoid bending your elbows during the movement.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control.
Exhale as you twist up and inhale as you lower down.
results.description: Dumbbell Straight Arm Twisting Sit-Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Straight Leg Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight just off the floor, and hold a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest. Lean back slightly to engage your core, keeping your back straight.
Rotate your torso to the right, moving the dumbbell towards the floor beside your right hip while keeping your legs extended just off the floor.
Rotate your torso back to the center, bringing the dumbbell back to center.
Continue rotating your torso to the left, moving the dumbbell towards the floor beside your left hip. Return to the center. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
tips: Avoid leaning back too far to prevent strain on your lower back.
Exhale as you twist to each side and inhale as you return to the center.
Keep your legs extended and together to maintain stability.
results.description: Dumbbell Straight Leg Russian Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Suitcase Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended vertically and your feet together. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest and extend your arms toward your legs.
Engage your core and lift your head, shoulders, and upper back while reaching the dumbbell toward your feet.
Pause briefly at the top and contract your abdominal muscles while keeping your legs raised and still.
Slowly lower your upper back toward the floor while maintaining the vertical leg position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your arms extended and the dumbbell securely held with both hands.
Keep your lower back controlled against the floor as you lower your torso.
Avoid swinging your arms or using momentum to complete the crunch.
Exhale as you crunch upward and inhale as you lower your upper body.
results.description: Dumbbell Suitcase Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell v-Up
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back with your legs extended straight and holding a dumbbell with both hands extended on the floor, arms fully extended.
Simultaneously lift your legs, upper body and dumbbell off the floor, bringing your legs and arms together to form a V-shape.
Reach the dumbbell towards your feet, keeping your arms and legs as straight as possible.
Slowly lower your legs, upper body and dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain straight arms and legs to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise.
Exhale as you lift into the V-up position and inhale as you lower back down.
Avoid jerking or using momentum; perform the movement in a controlled manner.
results.description: Dumbbell v-Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Elbow Push Plank Up
instructions: Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming an arch line from your head to your heels.
Push through your forearms to lift your elbows a few inches off the floor, keeping your fists on the floor.
Keep pressing through your forearms to raise your hips off the floor until your torso is straight, maintaining the plank position.
Lower your hips back down to the floor, followed by your elbows, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to prevent your forearms from slipping.
Ensure your elbows remain under your shoulders to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
results.description: Elbow Push Plank Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank
instructions: Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lift your elbows a few inches off the floor, keeping your forearms off the floor and fists on the floor.
Place your right hand on the floor, followed by your left hand, pushing your body up into a high plank position with your arms fully extended.
Lower your right hand back to the floor, followed by your left hand, returning to the starting position. Repeat the movement, alternating which arm you start with each time.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Avoid rotating your hips; keep them level to increase core stability.
Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to prevent your forearms and hands from slipping.
results.description: Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Exercise Ball Body Saw
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your forearms resting on an exercise ball and your body forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and slowly roll the ball a few inches away from your body.
Reverse the motion by rolling the ball closer to your forearms.
Continue the rolling motion for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a straight body line throughout.
tips: Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you move forward and inhaling as you move back.
Avoid allowing your lower back to arch; keep your spine in a neutral position.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to ensure stability and control during the movement.
results.description: Exercise Ball Body Saw is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Exercise Ball Sit Ups
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, leaning back so the ball supports your lower back and hips. Place your hands behind your head.
Engage your core and lift your upper body until vertical to the floor, performing a sit-up while keeping your chin slightly tucked and your back straight.
Lower your upper body back down to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in your core.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your lower back remains in contact with the exercise ball to support your spine and prevent injury.
Move slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to maximize muscle engagement.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lift your upper body and inhaling as you lower it.
Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands if they are placed behind your head; instead, use your core muscles to lift.
results.description: Exercise Ball Sit Ups is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Flat Knee Raise
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Place your hands lightly behind your head, and rest your head and shoulders against the floor.
Engage your core and lift both feet together, drawing your knees toward your chest while maintaining the bend in your legs.
Continue raising your knees until they are positioned above your abdomen, gently tilting your pelvis toward your ribs without lifting your upper back.
Slowly lower both legs until your feet return to the floor, maintaining control throughout the descent, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Support your head lightly without pulling on your neck with your hands.
Draw both knees upward together without swinging or using momentum.
Lower your feet slowly and touch the floor lightly before beginning the next repetition.
Exhale as you draw your knees toward your chest and inhale as you lower your feet.
results.description: Flat Knee Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

results.name: Flutter Kicks
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down. Place your hands under your hips for added support if needed.
Lift your legs off the floor a few inches, keeping them straight and close together.
Quickly alternate kicking your legs up and down in a small, controlled motion, engaging your core throughout the movement.
Continue the flutter kicks for the desired duration, maintaining a steady and controlled pace. Lower your legs back to the floor to complete the exercise.
tips: Move your legs in a controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you kick your legs and inhaling as you maintain the movement.
Avoid letting your lower back arch off the floor; keep it pressed down to prevent strain.
Adjust the height of your kicks to suit your fitness level and comfort, starting with smaller kicks and increasing the range of motion as you build strength.
results.description: Flutter Kicks is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.
